I am playing Monopoly.

I am analyzing the current game state to decide on post-turn actions. I have $1,102 and three properties: Mediterranean Avenue, B&O Railroad, and Pacific Avenue. Player 1 has $558 and owns Vermont, St. James, Indiana, Marvin Gardens, and Short Line.

I mapped the remaining properties by color. Most are unowned, with only a few exceptions.

Player 3 owns St. Charles and Penn RR. Player 4 has no properties and $1,475 cash. I have no monopolies and cannot build. Mortgaging is not useful with $1,102 on hand. I am weighing whether to trade for Baltic Avenue or additional railroads.

Player 1 has no near-monopolies. They own only one property per color group. A railroad monopoly would be strong but difficult to assemble without overpaying. A brown monopoly is cheap to build but offers low rent.

Baltic Avenue is not worth trading for. Player 4 has no properties to offer. A railroad trade would only yield two railroads, which is not transformative. Pacific Avenue is a strong green foothold and should be kept while North Carolina and Pennsylvania remain unowned.

I am leaning toward ending the turn to preserve cash for landing on properties. A trade with player 3 for Penn RR would likely be rejected, wasting one of the twenty allowed exchanges.
